implementation.dtype_layout_memory: Named precision policy 'attn-bfp8-mlp-bfp4-kv-bfp8-lofi': BFLOAT16 activations/residuals/norms, BFLOAT8_B attention weights (wqkv, attention gate, o_proj), BFLOAT4_B MLP weights (gate, up, down), BFLOAT8_B paged KV cache, LoFi math fidelity for both the decode and prefill projections. Every projection weight is a single DRAM WIDTH_SHARDED tensor (one shard per DRAM bank) shared by prefill and decode, so the per-layer weight footprint drops from 967,835,648 B (fused, BF16) to 314,802,176 B. Decode keeps the activation width-sharded in L1 across the whole layer on a 16-core boundary grid, with a phase-specific 26-core working grid for the MLP; the six decode projections are explicit MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastDRAMShardedProgramConfig dispatches with a per-(role, dtype) swept in0_block_w. Prefill activations stay DRAM interleaved and dispatch one of three kernels by row count: the DRAM-sharded matmul at exactly one M tile, an explicit 2D-multicast ttnn.linear from two tiles to the per-role crossover (<=1024 rows for the attention projections, <=512 for MLP gate/up, <=512 for mlp_down), and ttnn.experimental.minimal_matmul with swept per-shape blocking above it. Below 256 rows the four hidden-size prefill RMSNorms also run width-sharded in L1 on an exact 8x2 core rectangle rather than DRAM interleaved, because an interleaved rms_norm parallelises over tile rows and a short prefill starves it.
implementation.kv_cache_sizing: full max_seq_len per user (no bounded sliding-window cache in this stage)
implementation.decode_sdpa: paged_scaled_dot_product_attention_decode over the whole 11x10 compute grid with q_chunk_size=0 and k_chunk_size=0, i.e. the op chooses its chunking. This replaces the fused stage's inherited q=32/k=64 and is worth 19% of the decode step on the 'full' (NoPE) layer at context 131071; it is also what makes the BFP8 KV cache worth anything (1.4041 -> 1.2658 ms/token, against a wash at the fixed chunking).

extra_persistent_buffers.formula: 2 (cos, sin) * 131072 positions * head_dim(128) * 2 bytes (BF16), TILE layout
extra_persistent_buffers.note: Added by the fusing stage so prefill hands rotary_embedding_hf a pre-tilized table. The ROW_MAJOR tables the functional stage already carried are still needed for the decode-time per-user ttnn.embedding gather, so a sliding layer now holds both layouts. full (NoPE) layers hold neither. This does not change any capacity limit: it is 67 MB against this stage's 314.8 MB per-layer weight footprint on a 32 GB part (it was 968 MB when the fusing stage wrote this note; the optimized stage's precision policy cut the weights 3.07x, which makes the ratio worse but the absolute headroom unchanged).
extra_persistent_buffers.sliding_prefill_q_filler_formula: num_attention_heads(32) * sliding_window(2048) * head_dim(128) * 2 bytes (BF16), TILE layout -- one buffer per sliding layer, allocated lazily on the first multi-chunk sliding prefill and reused for every later chunk boundary. Tails shorter than the window slice this buffer rather than allocating their own, so the count is one regardless of how many distinct continuation offsets a caller uses. It replaces a per-boundary ttnn.zeros(device=...), which was a 16.78 MB host fill plus upload costing 2015.9 us each. Against a 314.8 MB per-layer weight footprint on a 32 GB part this changes no capacity limit; full (NoPE) layers hold none.

implementation.sliding_prefill_filler: The zero Q filler that the sliding-window prefill prepends at each internal chunk boundary is a single persistent window-length buffer, sliced for shorter continuation tails. ttnn.zeros(..., device=...) is a host buffer fill plus upload, not a device op, and at [1, 32, 2048, 128] BF16 = 16.78 MB it cost 2015.9 us of host time per boundary; the worst op-to-op gap in the two-chunk sliding prefill window is now 0.6 us.

prefill.reference_harness: reduced layer-level: the HF cache is filled with the K/V of every position before the compared block by the real MuseGlimmerTextAttention K/V path, then the real HF MuseGlimmerTextDecoderLayer runs that 32-query block against the full prefix. Two blocks are checked at 131072 - the last 32 rows and an interior block at row 65536 (first row of internal prefill chunk 9, entirely dependent on the 8th carried sliding window). A 131072-query HF forward is not tractable on CPU.

norm_shard_band.note: Below 256 rows the four hidden-size prefill RMSNorms run width-sharded in L1 on an exact 8x2 rectangle; above it they fall back to DRAM interleaved because the shard stops fitting L1 (512 rows overflows the circular-buffer budget by 33%). 256 is therefore the worst case inside the band, so PCC is asserted at 224/256 (inside) and 288/320 (outside) on both weight populations and both layer kinds. Worst real-weight check across the 16 cases: 0.996907.

batch.note: Ragged per-user prompt lengths 2000..3147 (straddling the 2048 sliding window) and per-user decode positions in one batched call. batch=13 is prime and larger than the 11-wide device grid, so it has no batch-core rectangle and exercises the decode head-concat's shape-agnostic fallback.
batch.device_op_ceiling_source: ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/experimental/transformer/nlp_create_qkv_heads_decode/device/nlp_create_qkv_heads_decode_device_operation.cpp:45-51 hard-caps num_users at 32, so decode batch is capped at 32 by the op, not by this layer. The largest tested batch (32) is therefore also the largest supported one; prefill is per-user and has no such cap.

continuation_prefill.note: Two start_pos-separated prefill calls compared against a single-shot HF prefill, then a decode past the join. sliding layers require the caller to thread sliding_kv_tail; the 1024 and 64 splits give a tail shorter than the 2048 window.

sliding_window_control.note: Direct probe against an explicit torch kv_idx > cur_pos - W mask over a permuted paged cache; the prefill op's window is pinned separately by doc/functional_decoder/sdpa_sliding_window_chunk_repro.py. Owned by the functional stage; the fused decoder uses the same decode SDPA op and window.

nonzero_cache_slot.note: Multi-chunk prefill plus decode off cache slot 2, exercising page-table row slicing and the chunked paged read from a non-zero row.

real_weights.note: This stage buys speed with weight precision, so the real checkpoint is the population the policy is selected on and the real-weight surface is much wider than the fused stage's single case: six prefill lengths x two layer kinds (including seq_len=1, which takes the one-tile DRAM-sharded prefill branch, and the non-aligned 2049/4097/8193 plus multi-chunk 12345), eight consecutive decode steps off the BFP8 cache, traced replay at batch 8, and a bounded head-to-head against the fused decoder. All real-weight checks clear the functional bar of 0.995; the count is tests.real_weight_checks and the worst is tests.min_pcc_real_weights (both regenerated by bench/refresh_context_contract.py, so this note does not carry a number that can drift). Tensors are loaded for exactly layer 0 / layer 3 out of the released safetensors shards with safe_open.

fp32_reference_control.note: Same weights and BF16-rounded inputs through an FP32 HF layer, so a BF16 error common-mode to both implementations cannot hide.

determinism.result: bit-identical (torch.equal) prefill and decode outputs for both layer kinds

stress.note: test_repeated_run_stress replays 64 decode steps across the boundary/MLP reshard pair and asserts PCC at steps 0, 16, 32, 48 and 63.

fallback_audit.note: test_no_host_fallback_in_forward traps ttnn.from_torch / ttnn.to_torch / ttnn.as_tensor and 13 torch entry points across a full prefill and decode pass.

optimized_path_asserted.note: PCC alone cannot tell an optimized dispatch from a fallback, so the shipped kernels and dtypes are asserted directly: test_decode_uses_dram_sharded_matmuls checks all six decode projections are DRAM-sharded program configs on width-sharded L1 activations and width-sharded DRAM weights with the swept in0_block_w and the policy's weight dtype; test_weight_dtype_policy_reaches_the_tensors checks the tensors themselves (OPT-013) and the single-copy property; test_prefill_uses_the_expected_dense_kernel checks all three prefill kernels at 32, 128, 2048 and 12345 rows; test_prefill_mcast_table_is_legal and test_decode_geometry_table_is_legal check the geometry tables host-side, including the 2D-multicast grid-width rule whose violation is silent.

byte_budget_at_full_context.kv_cache_formula: 2 (K,V) * num_key_value_heads(2) * head_dim(128) * 131072 tokens * 1.0625 bytes (BFLOAT8_B: 1024 mantissa + 64 exponent bytes per 32x32 tile)
byte_budget_at_full_context.layer_weight_formula: attention (6656*4608 wqkv + 6656*4096 attn_gate + 4096*6656 o_proj) * 1.0625 bytes (BFLOAT8_B) = 90,521,600 + MLP (3 * 6656*19968) * 0.5625 bytes (BFLOAT4_B: 512 mantissa + 64 exponent bytes per tile) = 224,280,576
byte_budget_at_full_context.note: The optimized layer is 3.07x smaller in weights and 1.88x smaller in KV cache than the fused one it replaces, so no capacity question is closer than before: the 131072-token context is supported and tested end to end. The 131072-token prefill activations are still bounded by the 8192-token internal prefill chunking.

notes: No capability reduction was taken by the optimized decoder stage; the advertised 131072-token context is supported and tested end to end (paged prefill fill + paged decode read) for both decoder-layer kinds, at batch up to 32, and at non-aligned logical lengths. The stage lowers weight and KV-cache precision, which costs accuracy against the fused decoder in a bounded and measured way (worst real-weight check 0.995079 against the 0.995 functional bar) and buys 2.51-2.56x traced decode.

performance.note: Two populations, both reported. 'device' is the Device Time column of tt-perf-report over a warmed, signposted Tracy window (microseconds, decode divided by its 8 trace replays); 'e2e' is warmed host wall time from bench/layer_ab.py, min of 3 rounds, measured in a separate run with no profiler attached. 'baseline' is the fused decoder measured in the same harness on the same host. All ten committed captures are free of dropped profiler markers.
performance.device_op_count_note: Decode op counts are identical to the fused stage: this stage changes dtype, matmul program config, activation layout and the SDPA chunking, not the decode topology. The 8192-token prefill chunk gains two ops, the ttnn.typecast calls that cast the K/V fill tensors to the BFP8 cache dtype (paged_fill_cache does no conversion of its own). The 128-row window gains eight more on top of that: the interleaved_to_sharded and sharded_to_interleaved that bracket each of the four sharded prefill norms, which are inside the measured candidate and still 1.19x faster than the interleaved norms they replace.
performance.context_scaling: sliding decode is context-independent (SDPA reads at most the 2048 window). full (NoPE) decode grows with context because its SDPA reads the whole cache, but far less than before: 1.049 -> 1.255 ms/token device between 2048 and 131071, against the fused stage's 2.687 -> 3.179.
performance.decode_roofline: One decode step streams 314,802,176 B of weights plus the KV the SDPA reads. At the ~512 GB/s this part peaks at, sliding@2048 (315.9 MB) has a 0.617 ms floor against 1.072 ms of device time, i.e. 58%; full@131071 (386.1 MB) has a 0.754 ms floor against 1.255 ms, 60%. The fused stage sat at 93% of its own roofline only because it moved 3.07x more bytes: with the weight traffic cut, the fixed costs are a much larger share. The gap is dominated by the three BFP4 MLP matmuls, which reach 286-297 GB/s (56-58% of peak) where the BFP8 attention matmuls reach 429-433 GB/s (84%) -- see the named limitation in doc/optimized_decoder/README.md.
performance.e2e_vs_device_gap: Traced decode end-to-end is within 11-19 us of device time at every context (1.7% at worst), so there is no material host term left in the decode loop. Note this is a cross-run subtraction: the device figure comes from a Tracy window and the e2e figure from a profiler-free run, because the profiler itself inflates dispatch gaps (the profiled decode window reports 56 us/replay of op-to-op gap, more than the 19 us the unprofiled e2e leaves room for). Untraced prefill keeps a larger host gap (37.8 ms device against 44.3 ms e2e at 8192 tokens); prefill is not traced in this stage, which owns a single decoder layer rather than a generator loop. The one host term that was removable has been removed -- see implementation.sliding_prefill_filler.
performance.fidelity_policy: LoFi for both the decode DRAM-sharded projections and the prefill dense projections, measured against HiFi2 on the identical dtype policy: HiFi2 is 69% slower in decode and 35% slower in prefill for +2.4e-4 of PCC. The RMSNorms keep the fused stage's HiFi4/math_approx_mode=False/fp32_dest_acc_en=True/packer_l1_acc=True uplift unchanged.

tests.acceptance_bar_note: The real-checkpoint bar is the functional stage's 0.995 and is the acceptance gate. The synthetic i.i.d.-Gaussian harness has its own documented 0.99 bar because BFP4 MLP weights cost that distribution 2.6x more accuracy than they cost the real checkpoint; $optimize OPT-012 is what makes that the right response, and doc/optimized_decoder/logs/bfp_block_range_probe.log refutes the three obvious mechanisms. It is deliberately not an expected-failure marker.

performance.note: Warmed, signposted Tracy windows; Device Time column from tt-perf-report --csv, microseconds. 8 trace replays per decode window; all ten committed captures (eight fused windows plus the two multi-chunk functional baselines) are free of dropped profiler markers. 'baseline' is the functional decoder measured the same way.
performance.context_scaling: sliding decode is context-independent (SDPA reads at most the 2048 window); full (NoPE) decode SDPA goes 36 us -> 529 us between 2048 and 131071.
performance.decode_roofline: One decode step streams 967,835,648 B of BF16 weights; at the 383 GB/s the six matmuls achieve that is 2.526 ms, i.e. 93 % of the 2.710 ms fused decode step. Further decode gains require moving fewer bytes (weight dtype) or a higher-efficiency matmul config.
performance.fidelity_policy: Unchanged from the functional stage: the prefill dense projections pin the same HiFi2 / fp32_dest_acc_en=False / packer_l1_acc=True compute-kernel config that ttnn.linear selects by default for BF16, so the before/after is a pure topology comparison. minimal_matmul's own default is more accurate (PCC 0.999994 vs 0.999947 vs FP32) and 2.3-2.5 ms slower per 8192-token prefill; that choice belongs to the optimized-decoder stage. ONE fidelity knob was turned: every RMSNorm runs HiFi4/math_approx_mode=False/fp32_dest_acc_en=True/packer_l1_acc=True instead of ttnn.rms_norm's own default (HiFi4/approx=True/fp32_acc=False/l1_acc=False, rmsnorm.cpp:16-20). Measured against float64: prefill norm 978.27 -> 991.78 us with max relative error 6.5e-2 -> 4.2e-3; sharded decode norm 15.53 -> 14.92 us (faster) and 1.0e-2 -> 4.8e-3. Cost ~54 us across the four hidden-size norms plus of order 25 us across the two per-head QK norms, i.e. 0.11-0.16 % of a 49,318 us prefill window, and nothing in decode; worth +3.3e-4 to +3.8e-4 of the accuracy gain where no matmul kernel changes (doc/fused_decoder/logs/norm_fidelity_control.log).

tests.accuracy_controls_note: All six prefill controls show the fused graph closer to the HF reference by +3.3e-4 to +1.2e-3 (the test allows no prefill regression at all). Five of six decode controls improve; one drifts by -4.6e-5, inside the 2e-4 BF16 re-association band the test allows for decode, which never changes matmul kernel. That band was 5e-4 until the prefill per-head QK norms took the same compute-kernel config as every other norm in the layer: those norms write the KV cache a decode step reads, and including them shrank the worst decode drift 10x.
